questions.questionText:
The municipal corporation has decided to impose a heavy penalty on residents who waste drinking water on washing private vehicles.

Conclusions:

II. A financial penalty is expected to deter the wasteful habit of citizens.

Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Only conclusion II follows

Step 2: Check Conclusion I: Does it follow naturally without importing outside speculation?
Step 3: Check Conclusion II: Does it introduce extreme claims or unmentioned comparisons?
Step 4: Select Both conclusion I and II follow.
questions.memoryTip: Rule of Thumb: A valid conclusion is an inevitable consequence, not an imaginative possibility.

Conclusions:
I. Higher borrowing costs can help moderate aggregate demand and curb inflation.
II. Inflation will immediately drop to zero percent in the upcoming month.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
Only conclusion I follows
Only conclusion II follows
questions.hint: Evaluate whether the second conclusion makes an impossible guarantee.
questions.explanation: Increasing interest rates to curb inflation reflects the economic rationale that elevated cost of credit dampens excessive demand (Conclusion I). Claiming inflation will drop to zero is absurd and ungrounded in the text (Conclusion II fails).
solutionSteps: Step 1: Read the statement carefully and treat it as 100% true.
Step 2: Check Conclusion I: Does it follow naturally without importing outside speculation?
Step 3: Check Conclusion II: Does it introduce extreme claims or unmentioned comparisons?
Step 4: Select Only conclusion I follows.
questions.memoryTip: Rule of Thumb: A valid conclusion is an inevitable consequence, not an imaginative possibility.
